test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)?

1. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita introduces community service as a punishment for minor offences.

2. The scope of summary trials has been limited to only serious offences under the new law.

3. The reformative approach aims to ensure societal reintegration of offenders.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) introduces **community service as a punishment for minor offences**, focusing on restorative justice mechanisms.
 
• The reformative approach of the BNS aims to ensure **societal reintegration of offenders**, reducing recidivism through rehabilitation.
 
• The scope of summary trials remains focused on **minor offences**, contrary to the incorrect statement suggesting it is limited to serious offences.
 
• The BNS is part of the Indian government’s broader efforts to modernize criminal laws while aligning them with constitutional and human rights principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Community Service:** A reformative punishment where offenders contribute constructively to society, reducing reliance on incarceration for minor offences.
 
• **Reformative Justice:** A principle focusing on rehabilitating offenders and reintegrating them into society rather than solely penalizing them.
 
• **Summary Trials:** A legal procedure for expeditious resolution of cases involving minor offences, ensuring quick justice delivery.
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita:** A proposed legal framework that seeks to replace the Indian Penal Code (IPC), aligning with modern jurisprudence and societal needs.
 
• **Criminal Justice Reforms in India:** The BNS is part of the government’s initiative to modernize outdated laws, ensuring they are more equitable, efficient, and people-centric.
